page: Microsoft Azure F64as_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance belonging to the Fasv6 series, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built around AMD EPYC 9V74 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a nominal clock frequency of 3.7 GHz without multithreading overhead. System memory totals 256.0 GB, maintaining an allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration features 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per segment, alongside architectural instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512-VNNI, AVX512-BF16, and AES cryptography acceleration. The server provision includes zero local disk storage and zero discrete GPUs, relying entirely on remote storage infrastructure.

Benchmark measurements reflect high processing capacity across parallel execution workloads. In stress-ng evaluations, the multi-core score reaches 196,900.41, placing it in the top decile, while single-core performance registers 3,080.88. Geekbench scores further confirm this execution strength, recording 25,348.0 for multi-core tests and 2,099.0 for single-core tasks. In application-specific assessments, the instance achieved 73,332.0 in Clang software compilation and 99,875.0 in ray tracing, both residing in the top tier. Cryptographic and vector workloads are supported by extended instruction performance, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 91,536.52 and extended instruction evaluation of 113,220.8.

Data throughput characteristics show competitive scaling under both memory-bound and transactional pressures. Cached read memory bandwidth achieves 9,339.97 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads and writes register at 289.01 GB/sec and 153.61 GB/sec respectively. Redis throughput reaches 132.21 million SET operations per second, ranking within the top tier. CPU-driven inference benchmarking demonstrates strong capacity for lightweight transformer execution, delivering 5,674.68 prompt processing tokens per second on small models and 48.78 text generation tokens per second on medium 7B parameter models.

The absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires external disk attachments, which introduces storage architecture tradeoffs for I/O-intensive pipelines. In contrast, the dedicated 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core topology eliminates hyperthreading contention, delivering consistent performance for parallel software compilation, continuous integration build farms, batch processing, rendering, and in-memory key-value caching.
description: Microsoft Azure F64as_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running on 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processors. Equipped with 256.0 GB of memory at 4.0 GB per core, this instance operates on the x86_64 architecture and supports advanced instruction extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic offloads. It contains zero local storage and no GPU hardware, depending on network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmark results place the instance in the top tier for multi-threaded performance, demonstrating 196,900.41 on stress-ng multi-core and 25,348.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Software build tasks via Clang, ray tracing, and in-memory key-value processing via Redis also register top-decile performance. Because the instance provides dedicated physical execution threads without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers reliable throughput for compute-intensive batch processing, CI/CD compilation, distributed simulations, and application server clusters.
